incident.what: The operator, asked to choose between options on well-formed decision cards, said the explanation was still not clear enough: 'the things that should be loud must be loud, or I cannot see how to choose.' Every required element was present; the choice itself was not visually dominant.
incident.signal: Direct feedback after receiving cards that passed the five-element check.

root_cause: The five-element rule guaranteed content, not salience. A reader under load scans for what is emphasised; if nothing is, they must read everything.

law.text: On a decision card, the choice is the loudest thing on the page: a bold one-glance line directly under the heading; every option word bold; the recommendation bolds exactly one option word from the table. Content without salience fails.
checks: first line under the heading is bold and states the choice
all option words in the table are bold
recommendation contains one bold option word matching the table

notes: Refines law-006 (five elements, max three cards). Laws stay parallel; this one adds salience to the same incident class.
